reminder.notes:
Reminder 2.25.1 - Diagnostics finally have somewhere to go

The app has recorded technical failures for a long time and has never once been
able to send them. They were posted to a Tailscale hostname, on a tailnet no
phone was ever a member of, with no server behind it. Every incident queued on
the device to its hundred-item cap and was then dropped.

Nothing about the reporting changed here, because nothing about it was wrong.
It now has an address that exists.

### Features

- Diagnostics are sent to diagnostics.pnsjy.in, which is a real relay reached
  through the same tunnel as everything else. Consent and content are unchanged:
  allow-listed technical failures only, never reminder text, location, files or
  account state.

### Bug fixes

- The relay address pointed at a tailnet host that resolves nowhere. Every
  incident this app has ever recorded was queued and discarded.
- Removed two unused constants naming a Google Sheet that incidents do not go
  to. Nothing read them, and anyone reading the file would reasonably have
  believed otherwise.

### Notes

DIAGNOSTICS_RELAY still overrides the address at build time, so a debug build
can point at a local instance.

### Toolchain

The build was broken before this release and could not produce an APK at all.
build_runner crashed inside the analyzer with "Missing implementation of
visitDotShorthandPropertyAccess". The cause was the Flutter SDK itself: its
services/platform_views.dart declares a parameter default using dot-shorthand
syntax, and the pinned analyzer 7.6.0 has no visitor for that node, so anything
summarising package:flutter/services.dart died.

riverpod_generator was what pinned that analyzer, and this app has zero
@riverpod annotations - it was doing no work and blocking the toolchain.
Removing it and riverpod_annotation freed analyzer to 13.3.0 and drift_dev to
2.34.x. flutter_riverpod stays on 2.6.1, so nothing about how the app builds
state changed.

Deprecated Flutter APIs were migrated as part of getting the build green:
Switch.activeColor to activeThumbColor, and both Radio groups onto RadioGroup
ancestors. The delete-scope dialog had no tests at all despite being the screen
that decides whether one occurrence or a whole repeating reminder is destroyed;
it has five now.

twinclean.notes:
Show the app version and PNSJY branding in Settings

Settings now ends with the current app version and the PNSJY store branding, so every
PNSJY app presents the same footer.

### Features

- The Settings screen now shows the installed app version and a PNSJY brand footer as its
  last two items, consistent across all PNSJY apps.

### Bug fixes

No user-facing bug fixes in this release.

family.notes:
## Bug fixes

- **Fixed the app being told there was no update when there was one.** The list of published versions is cached for ten minutes by the network it comes from, and the app was reading whichever copy it was handed. So for at least ten minutes after a release — and longer if a phone or network held the file — checking for updates confidently reported that the current version was the newest. The app now always asks for a fresh copy.

  An update check that answers wrongly is worse than one that does not run: it stops you looking.

taashclub.notes:
Taash Club 1.10.0 - You deal, you shuffle

Every table now shows who is dealing, and when it is your deal you can shuffle
the pack - as many times as you like.

### Features

- Har table par dikhega kaun baant raha hai. Aur jab aapki baari ho baantne ki,
  "Phento" dabao - jitni baar chaho. Har baar patte sach mein badal jaate hain.
- Teeno games mein: 3-2-5, Kali Begum aur Gochi.

### Bug fixes

- None. This adds to the deal; it changes nothing about how any game is played.

### Notes

The shuffle is real, and that mattered more than it sounds. It would have been
easy to animate a riffle and deal exactly the same cards - it would look right,
feel right, and nobody playing could ever have caught it.

The app already deals with a provably-fair shuffle: the server commits to a
secret seed before the deal and reveals it afterwards, so it cannot arrange the
cards. Until now the other half of that seed was worked out from who was sitting
at the table - predictable, with nobody actually contributing anything. Your
shuffle now mixes fresh randomness into it, after the server has already
committed. So the server cannot arrange the deal and cannot predict it either,
and your contribution shows up in the seed on the fairness screen where you can
check it.

Offline there is no server to commit to anything, so shuffling simply deals
again from a fresh pack. Same gesture, same effect on the cards.

Shuffling is only offered between hands, to whoever is about to deal. Mid-hand
it would either do nothing or look like it did something.

cards.notes:
Cards 2.5.2 - Buildable again, and finally listed in the store

Cards could not be built at all, and separately had never been listed in PNSJY
Store - so it was publishing releases that nobody could find.

### Features

- Cards ab PNSJY Store mein dikhega. Install aur update wahin se, aur nayi
  version aane par notification bhi.

### Bug fixes

- None in the app itself. Scanning, the vault and the encryption are unchanged.

### Notes

Two build problems, neither of them in this app's own code.

android/gradle.properties pinned org.gradle.java.home to an Android Studio path
that only exists on a machine with Android Studio installed in the default
place. On the build server there is none, so Gradle refused to start. No other
app in this fleet pins it; this one no longer does either.

flutter_tesseract_ocr - the OCR fallback for Google-free ROMs - calls jcenter()
in its build file, which Gradle has removed, and pins an old Android Gradle
Plugin. Either one stops the build before a single file compiles. Version
0.4.31 is the last release that package will ever have, so there was nothing to
upgrade to.

Rather than drop the fallback, a patched copy now lives in third_party/. It is
byte-identical to the published package apart from that one build file, where
the plugin's own buildscript block is removed - a Flutter plugin does not need
one, because the host app supplies the Android Gradle Plugin and the
repositories. Vendoring is what makes the fix survive: the package cache is not
ours and gets wiped.

Scanning on Google-free devices therefore still works, which it would not have
if the dependency had simply been deleted.
